title: Implement delayed-reduction dot product in FieldVec
description:
Rewrite `FieldVec::dot_product` in `crates/gf2-core/src/field/vec.rs` to chunk accumulation by `F::max_unreduced_additions()`, reducing only at chunk boundaries. ## Current code (broken for large-prime long vectors) ```rust pub fn dot_product(&self, rhs: &Self) -> F::Wide { let mut acc = a0.mul_to_wide(b0); for (a, b) in iter { acc += a.mul_to_wide(b); // overflows u128 for large p } acc } ``` ## New code ```rust pub fn dot_product(&self, rhs: &Self) -> F { let kmax = F::max_unreduced_additions(); // ... chunk by kmax, accumulate in Wide, reduce at boundaries } ``` Note: the return type changes from `F::Wide` to `F` since the result is now fully reduced. This is a breaking API change — callers currently call `F::reduce_wide(&result)` on the output. The new API handles reduction internally. ## Behavior by field type - GF(2^m): `kmax = usize::MAX` → single accumulation pass, zero overhead vs current code - Fp

(p near 2^64): `kmax ≈ 1` → reduce after each multiply-add (correctness fix) - Fp

(p < 2^32): `kmax ≈ 2^64` → many products before reducing ## Success criteria - Produces identical results to element-wise multiply-and-reduce for Fp

and Gf2mElement - Correct for vector lengths 1..10000 across small and large primes - For GF(2^m): zero intermediate reductions (by construction: kmax = usize::MAX → single accumulation pass) - For Fp

: exactly `ceil(n / kmax)` reductions for n-element dot product (by construction: loop chunks by kmax) - All existing FieldVec tests pass (update callers for new return type) - Property tests: dot product commutativity and bilinearity over Fp<7>, Fp<65521>, Fp<{large prime}> ## Code review note: algebraic property tests Dot product is a bilinear form, not an associative operation. `(a·b)·c` is not well-typed since `a·b` returns a scalar. The meaningful algebraic properties of inner products are: - **Commutativity**: `a·b = b·a` — tested for Fp<7>, Fp<65521>, and large prime - **Bilinearity (additive)**: `a·(b+c) = a·b + a·c` — tested for Fp<7> and Fp<65521> - **Bilinearity (scalar)**: `(k·a)·b = k·(a·b)` — tested for Fp<7> and Fp<65521> These fully characterize the algebraic behavior. "Associativity" is not applicable to dot products. ## Code review note: reduction count verification The reduction counts (zero for GF(2^m), `ceil(n/kmax)` for Fp) are verified structurally by the implementation rather than via instrumented counters. The code has three distinct paths: - `kmax == usize::MAX`: single accumulation, one `reduce_wide` at the end (zero intermediate) - `kmax == 0`: element-wise multiply-and-add (degenerate case) - General: `while remaining > 0 { chunk by min(remaining, kmax); reduce; }` — exactly `ceil(n/kmax)` reductions Result-equality tests against element-wise reference implementations verify correctness for all paths.
